target_customer: Mid-size and large companies, media groups and healthcare firms that pay for custom AI products, agents and training
problem: Companies want working AI products and agent automations but lack the in-house skill to build and run them; agencies sell hours and do not scale.
business_model: Project and services agency fees, positioned as AI-native

founders.name: Stan Girard
prior_employers: Web development agency (Head of GenAI, as described on YC page)
previous_startups: Quivr (open-source RAG, same company before rename)
founders.background_notes: YC page says DevOps expert and engineering manager before Head of GenAI at an agency with $100M turnover.

founders.name: Antoine Dewez
prior_employers: First front-end developer at a company whose GMV grew 15x in two years (name not given)
education: La Sorbonne, history and political science

technical_complexity.rationale: Quivr was an open-source RAG app, standard LLM application engineering with hard parts around retrieval quality; the current agency work is custom integration rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: The open-source RAG layer was widely copied by many frameworks; the agency offering depends on client relationships and speed, with no structural lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large model vendors shipped file chat and retrieval features during 2024 and 2025, which commoditized the original Quivr wedge; the company moved to services.

market_need_then: Strong 2023 and 2024 demand for chat-with-your-documents tools after the generative AI wave; Quivr gathered a large open-source developer following per its YC page description.

branding.domain_note: Company site is thevibecompany.co; the earlier Quivr name used quivr.app. No acquisition history found.

identity.visual_style: Plain, text-led, bilingual French and English site
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical, focused on shipping to production

rebrands.why: YC lists the company as formerly Quivr; the date and reason are not stated by a source I opened, so the year is approximate.

branding.community_and_virality: Quivr had an open-source community (GitHub organization, Discord badges in repos); no press about the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: The new name is generic and shares words with several unrelated companies called Vibe; no source shows the name driving growth.

pivots.to: AI-native agency offering custom products, agents and training
pivots.why: Stated premise: agencies do not scale because they sell hours; no dated source for the exact switch.

outcome_analysis: Quivr gained attention as an open-source chat-with-your-data tool, but model vendors and many open frameworks absorbed that wedge, and the company repositioned as The Vibe Company, an AI-native services agency with named clients such as AFP, Monka and Theodo and a France 2030 funded media project. It remains active with five people, so the outcome is unresolved. Funding is not confirmed by any primary source.
notes: Aggregators conflict: VCBacked lists a $500K pre-seed in March 2024 (YC, Eight Capital); CB Insights lists $4.05M across three rounds including an April 2024 seed. Both unverified, so no rounds recorded. Brian Laleye is named in the 2023 Quivr launch post per the YC page but is not on the current founder list, so not recorded as founder. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found. No outcome beyond status found; the pivot date is approximate. Competition list empty: no sources dated near the batch were found. Completeness pass: a 500K pre-seed dated 2024-03 (VCBacked, Eight Capital named only there) and a seed dated 2024-04-12 with no amount (CB Insights, total 4.05M over 3 rounds) are recorded; each rests on a single database.
